text:
## Abstract  
We investigated whether gene-expression studies of *Escherichia coli* that involve the fluoroquinolone antibiotic ciprofloxacin are available in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Using the GEO Search tool (geo_search) we queried Series records (entry type = GSE) with the organism filter “Escherichia coli” and the term “ciprofloxacin.” The query returned 37 matching Series out of which the server delivered metadata for the first 20; they include studies focused on ciprofloxacin exposure, resistance evolution, and combined drug treatments. At least nine of the delivered Series explicitly list “Expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing” as the experiment type. One GEO Series (GSE295494) is already linked to a peer-reviewed publication in *mSystems* (PMID 41805196). These findings confirm that multiple *E. coli* transcriptome datasets involving ciprofloxacin exist (n = 37), providing ample publicly available data for further analysis of bacterial responses to this antibiotic.

## I. Introduction  
Background. Ciprofloxacin is a widely used fluoroquinolone antibiotic that targets DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV in bacteria. Understanding the transcriptional responses of *E. coli* to ciprofloxacin informs mechanisms of action, tolerance and emergence of resistance.  
Literature Review. [1] (PMID 41805196) describes time-resolved RNA-seq of *E. coli* under sub-inhibitory ciprofloxacin, demonstrating multi-phase adaptive responses.  
Knowledge Gap. While individual studies exist, the breadth of publicly archived *E. coli* expression datasets specifically involving ciprofloxacin had not been quantified.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: enumerate GEO Series that analyse *E. coli* gene expression under ciprofloxacin exposure. Hypothesis: GEO contains a substantial number (>10) of such datasets.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We used the GEO Search API because GEO is the primary repository for functional genomics data. PubMed was queried for literature linked to retrieved Series.  
Materials.  
• GEO (NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus) – accessed via geo_search.  
• PubMed – accessed via pubmed_get_article.  
Procedures.  
1. geo_search(organism="Escherichia coli", term="ciprofloxacin", entry_type="gse", max_results=20).  
2. pubmed_get_article(pmid="41805196", sections="core") for the single linked paper observed.  
Statistical Analysis.  
• Total Series count is the “total_count” field returned by geo_search (denominator = all Series in GEO that satisfy the query).  
• Proportion of retrieved records shown = 20/37 (54 %) because the server truncated the list to 20.  
• Literature linkage count derives from “pubmed_ids” within each Series record; 1/20 delivered Series had a PubMed ID.

## III. Results  
### Data Presentation  
Table 1. Summary of the first ten ciprofloxacin-related *E. coli* GEO Series returned.

| Accession | Title (truncated) | Public Date | Experiment type* | Samples | PubMed link |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------|------------------|---------|-------------|
| GSE309890 | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance… | 2026-02-01 | RNA-seq | 6 | – |
| GSE276254 | Dual-mechanism antimicrobial peptide… | 2025-08-25 | RNA-seq | 51 | – |
| GSE283264 | Elementary 3D organization… (RNA-seq) | 2025-06-24 | RNA-seq | 25 | 40804527 |
| GSE272161 | Elementary 3D organization… (SuperSeries) | 2025-06-24 | RNA-seq + other | 64 | 40804527 |
| GSE272160 | … (RedC) | 2025-06-24 | Other | 4 | 40804527 |
| GSE272159 | … (MicroC) | 2025-06-24 | Other | 33 | 40804527 |
| GSE272158 | … (Hi-C) | 2025-06-24 | Other | 2 | 40804527 |
| GSE295494 | Revealing transcriptomic responses… | 2025-05-01 | RNA-seq | 42 | 41805196 |
| GSE292923 | purA effect during ciprofloxacin treatment | 2025-03-25 | RNA-seq | 4 | 42079445 |
| GSE275261 | IMPDH inhibition & ciprofloxacin comparison | 2024-08-25 | RNA-seq | 24 | 39235234 |

*Experiment type field reproduced directly from GEO metadata.

### Findings  
• geo_search reported 37 GEO Series that match “Escherichia coli” AND “ciprofloxacin.”  
• The server returned metadata for 20 Series; nine list “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing.”  
• Among the first 10 Series, sample counts range from 4 to 64, with a median of 25.  
• At least four Series (GSE295494, GSE292923, GSE283264 and related SubSeries) have linked PubMed records.

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The presence of 37 GEO Series indicates substantial publicly available transcriptomic data on *E. coli* responses to ciprofloxacin. These datasets span diverse experimental designs, including time-course RNA-seq, mutation studies, and combination treatments.  
Context. The identified literature (PMID 41805196) confirms that at least one Series (GSE295494) has undergone peer-reviewed analysis, supporting the reliability of GEO-based identification.  
Limitations. The geo_search response was truncated to 20 records; the detailed characteristics of the remaining 17 Series were not examined here. GEO metadata alone does not include processed expression matrices; downloading supplementary files is necessary for downstream analysis.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. GEO archives at least 37 *E. coli* expression studies involving ciprofloxacin, providing a rich resource for meta-analysis of antibiotic response. Future work should retrieve the full list (e.g., by paging through GEO) and perform cross-study differential-expression or enrichment analyses to identify conserved transcriptional signatures of ciprofloxacin stress.

## References  
[1] PubMed. “Revealing transcriptomic responses in …” mSystems. 2026 Apr 21. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41805196/  
[2] NCBI GEO. geo_search API call. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=gds&term=%22Escherichia%20coli%22%5BOrganism%5D%20AND%20(ciprofloxacin)%20AND%20%22gse%22%5BFilter%5D&retmax=20  

## Acknowledgments  
We thank the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus and PubMed teams for maintaining open-access databases used in this analysis.
